final_candidates.decision_summary: Best evolutionary support among candidates, perfect sequence-model plausibility, and solid structural compatibility; moderate toxin signal is acceptable for replication fitness.
Strong sequence support and good structural compatibility with moderate evolutionary tolerance and high coverage.
Conservative hydrophobic substitution with strong structural and sequence-model support despite low natural conservation.

stop_reason.detail: All 4 tool calls were used and additional evidence is unlikely to change the final top-3.

history.rationale: Removes the N-linked glycan at E-N154, which can alter receptor usage and cell tropism; glycan-loss variants often show altered replication fitness in flaviviruses.
Strong sequence plausibility and moderate structure compatibility, but low MSA coverage at this glycosylation-site position and functional uncertainty about glycan loss keep it out of the top tier.
N154Q has negligible evolutionary support and only moderate structural compatibility at a glycosylation-sensitive position, making it unlikely to improve replication fitness.

rejection.reason: N154Q has negligible evolutionary support and only moderate structural compatibility at a glycosylation-sensitive position, making it unlikely to improve replication fitness.

history.rationale: Modifies the glycosylation motif and local charge; may affect virus assembly or infectivity without eliminating the side chain entirely.
Very strong structure compatibility and high sequence plausibility, but low evolutionary coverage and glycosylation-site functional risk prevent a higher rank.
N154D has excellent structural and sequence-model support, but weak evolutionary support and glycosylation-site risk keep it below the top three.
Adds a positive charge in domain III, potentially enhancing glycosaminoglycan binding and cell-culture replication fitness.
Positive evolutionary frequency, maximal sequence plausibility, and good structural compatibility make this a robust viability-preserving candidate.
T335K has moderate evolutionary tolerance with good coverage, strong sequence support, and solid structural compatibility.
Surface-exposed domain III loop residue; substitution to lysine may increase heparin sulfate binding and viral entry efficiency.

Highest natural evolutionary frequency, maximal sequence plausibility, and good structural compatibility make this the strongest viability-preserving DIII candidate, with only a mild borderline-toxicity concern.
A310K retains the strongest evolutionary support among active candidates and has high sequence/structure plausibility; the slightly elevated toxin signal is not disqualifying for replication fitness.
Charge reversal in domain III could strengthen interactions with negatively charged cell-surface molecules and improve replication in vitro.
Charge-reversal mutation has zero natural occurrence, poor structural compatibility, and pushes the local peptide into toxic territory; rejected despite high PLM score.

rejection.reason: Charge-reversal mutation has zero natural occurrence, poor structural compatibility, and pushes the local peptide into toxic territory; rejected despite high PLM score.

history.rationale: Removes a negative charge in the domain III receptor-binding region, potentially reducing electrostatic repulsion during entry.
Zero evolutionary occurrence and poor structure compatibility for a glycine substitution in DIII make it unlikely to preserve fitness.

rejection.reason: Zero evolutionary occurrence and poor structure compatibility for a glycine substitution in DIII make it unlikely to preserve fitness.

history.rationale: Introduces a positive charge into a solvent-exposed domain III loop, which may enhance attachment and entry fitness.
Zero evolutionary occurrence and severely poor structural compatibility indicate this substitution is not viable.

rejection.reason: Zero evolutionary occurrence and severely poor structural compatibility indicate this substitution is not viable.

history.rationale: Conservative retention of positive charge at a surface-exposed domain III position; may preserve stability while subtly modulating receptor binding.
Conservative K->R substitution with moderate evolutionary frequency and solid structure compatibility is likely to be neutral-to-viable.
K394R is a conservative substitution with moderate evolutionary support and good structural compatibility.
Conservative hydrophobic substitution in domain III; may be tolerated and could modestly affect local packing or receptor interaction.
High sequence plausibility and the best structure compatibility among DIII substitutions support a conservative hydrophobic change, despite low natural occurrence.
V330L is retained because its strong structural and sequence-model support offset low evolutionary conservation; the conservative hydrophobic change may preserve fitness.
Located in the E stem region; V to M substitution has been observed in natural ZIKV lineages and may affect fusion or assembly fitness.
Weak evolutionary support, very poor sequence-model plausibility, and no usable structure score make this stem/TM-proximal substitution unlikely to preserve fitness.
